bottom_line: In CHARISMA, clopidogrel plus aspirin vs placebo plus aspirin did not significantly reduce the primary composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes (relative risk, 0.93; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.83 to 1.05).
implications: These results support that, in the overall trial population, clopidogrel plus aspirin was not significantly more effective than placebo plus aspirin for the primary composite end point (0.93; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.83 to 1.05; P = 0.22). They also show more moderate bleeding with clopidogrel plus aspirin (2.1 percent vs. 1.3 percent; P<0.001) and no statistically significant increase in severe bleeding (1.7 percent vs. 1.3 percent; P = 0.09).

major_points.text: 15,603 patients with clinically evident cardiovascular disease or multiple risk factors were randomly assigned to clopidogrel 75 mg/day plus low-dose aspirin vs placebo plus low-dose aspirin; median follow-up 28 months.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned 15,603 patients with either clinically evident cardiovascular disease or multiple risk factors to receive clopidogrel (75 mg per day) plus low-dose aspirin (75 to 162 mg per day) or placebo plus low-dose aspirin and followed them for a median of 28 months.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy endpoint was first occurrence of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was the first occurrence of myocardial infarction, stroke (of any cause), or death from cardiovascular causes (including hemorrhage).

major_points.text: Primary endpoint was not significantly different between groups: 6.8% vs 7.3% (RR 0.93; 95% CI 0.83–1.05; P=0.22).
Severe bleeding (GUSTO) was numerically higher with clopidogrel plus aspirin: 1.7% vs 1.3% (RR 1.25; 95% CI 0.97–1.61; P=0.09), and moderate bleeding was increased: 2.1% vs 1.3% (RR 1.62; P<0.001).

subgroups.text: Analyses of the primary end point were performed in several prospectively defined subgroups, including symptomatic vs asymptomatic patients.
subgroups.quote: Analyses of the primary end point were also performed in several prospectively defined sub- groups. The subgroups included symptomatic pa- tients (defined as patients enrolled on the basis of established cardiovascular disease) as compared with asymptomatic patients

subgroups.text: Among 3284 asymptomatic patients, primary events were 6.6% with clopidogrel vs 5.5% with placebo (P=0.20).
subgroups.quote: Among the 3284 asymptomatic patients, there was a 20 percent relative increase in the rate of primary events with clopidogrel (6.6 percent, vs. 5.5 percent with placebo; P = 0.20)

subgroups.text: Among 12,153 symptomatic patients, primary endpoint was 6.9% vs 7.9% (relative risk 0.88; 95% CI 0.77 to 0.998; P=0.046).
subgroups.quote: among the 12,153 symptomatic patients, there was a mar- ginally significant reduction in the primary end point with clopidogrel (6.9 percent, vs. 7.9 percent with placebo; relative risk, 0.88; 95 percent con- fidence interval, 0.77 to 0.998; P = 0.046).

subgroups.text: Interaction term for differential treatment response between asymptomatic and symptomatic patients was marginally significant (P=0.045).
subgroups.quote: The in- teraction term for this analysis, when the differ- ential treatment response in asymptomatic and symptomatic patients was examined, was margin- ally significant (P = 0.045).

subgroups.text: Asymptomatic subgroup had higher death from cardiovascular causes with clopidogrel: 3.9% vs 2.2% (P=0.01).
subgroups.quote: the rate of death from cardiovascular causes among those assigned to clopidogrel (3.9 percent vs. 2.2 percent, respectively; P = 0.01).

harms.text: Severe bleeding occurred in 1.7% vs 1.3% (RR 1.25; P=0.09).
harms.quote: The rate of the primary safety end point (severe bleeding according to the GUSTO definition) was 1.7 percent in the clopidogrel group and 1.3 per- cent in the placebo group (relative risk, 1.25; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.97 to 1.61; P = 0.09).

harms.text: Moderate bleeding occurred in 2.1% vs 1.3% (RR 1.62; P<0.001).
harms.quote: The rate of moderate bleeding was 2.1 percent in the clopidogrel group, as compared with 1.3 per- cent in the placebo group (relative risk, 1.62; 95 percent confidence interval, 1.27 to 2.08; P<0.001).

harms.text: One documented nonfatal case of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura occurred among clopidogrel-treated patients; patient died one month later from end-stage chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
harms.quote: There was one documented nonfatal case of thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura among the clopidogrel-treated patients; this patient died one month later from end-stage chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

harms.text: Treatment was permanently discontinued by 20.4% vs 18.2% (P<0.001).
harms.quote: Treatment was per- manently discontinued by 20.4 percent of the pa- tients in the clopidogrel group, as compared with 18.2 percent in the placebo group (P<0.001).

harms.text: Discontinued treatment because of an adverse event: 4.8% vs 4.9% (P=0.67).
harms.quote: total of 4.8 percent of the patients in the clopido- grel group and 4.9 percent of those in the placebo group discontinued treatment because of an ad- verse event (P = 0.67).

inclusion_criteria.text: Patients were eligible if they were 45 years of age or older.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were eligible to enroll in the trial if they were 45 years of age or older

inclusion_criteria.text: Eligible patients had multiple atherothrombotic risk factors or documented coronary, cerebrovascular, or symptomatic peripheral arterial disease.
inclusion_criteria.quote: and had one of the following conditions: multiple atherothrombotic risk factors, documented coronary disease, documented cerebrovascular disease, or documented symptomatic peripheral arterial disease.

exclusion_criteria.text: Excluded if taking oral antithrombotic medications or long-term NSAIDs (COX-2 inhibitors permitted).
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were excluded from the trial if they were taking oral antithrombotic medications or nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs on a long- term basis (although cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitors were permitted).

exclusion_criteria.text: Excluded if investigator judged there were established indications for clopidogrel therapy (e.g., recent acute coronary syndrome).
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were also excluded if, in the judgment of the investigator, they had established indications for clopidogrel therapy (such as a recent acute coronary syndrome).

exclusion_criteria.text: Patients scheduled for revascularization could not enroll until completed, and were excluded if they were considered to require clopidogrel after revascularization.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients who were scheduled to undergo a revascularization were not allowed to enroll until the procedure had been completed; such patients were excluded if they were considered to require clopidogrel after revascularization.

analysis_methods.text: Sample size and event target planned to detect a 20% relative risk reduction with 90% power at two-sided 0.05, assuming 3.1% annual event rate in control group.
analysis_methods.quote: We estimated that 15,200 patients (7600 per group) and 1040 primary events would be necessary to detect a 20 percent relative risk reduction in the primary efficacy end point, with 90 percent power at the two-sided 0.05 significance level

analysis_methods.text: Intention-to-treat analysis including outcomes from randomization to a common study end date (August 29, 2005).
analysis_methods.quote: Data were analyzed on an intention-to-treat basis, with the inclusion of all patients according to their randomly assigned treatment group and the inclusion of outcomes occurring from random- ization to a common study end date (August 29, 2005).

analysis_methods.text: Primary efficacy compared using a two-sided log-rank test; hazard ratio estimated using Cox proportional-hazards model.
analysis_methods.quote: The primary efficacy of clopidogrel as com- pared with placebo was assessed with the use of a two-sided log-rank test. The treatment effect as measured by the hazard ratio (the relative risk) and its associated 95 percent confidence interval was estimated with the use of the Cox propor- tional-hazards model.

analysis_methods.text: No adjustments for multiple comparisons were made.
analysis_methods.quote: No adjustments for multiple com- parisons were made.

analysis_methods.text: Type I error control: 0.001 at each interim analysis, preserving 0.049 for final analysis.
analysis_methods.quote: A two-sided type I error of 0.001 was used at each analysis. A type I error of 0.049 was preserved for the final analysis.

trial_conduct.text: Trial approved by institutional ethics committees at each participating institution and appropriate national ethics committees.
trial_conduct.quote: The trial was approved by the institutional ethics committee of each participating institution as well as the appropriate national ethics committees.

trial_conduct.text: Written informed consent was obtained before randomization.
trial_conduct.quote: After providing written informed consent, pa- tients were randomly assigned either to clopido- grel (75 mg per day) plus low-dose aspirin

trial_conduct.text: Primary trial end points were adjudicated by a blinded clinical events committee.
trial_conduct.quote: All primary trial end points were adjudicated by the clinical events committee, whose members were unaware of patients’ treatment assignments.

trial_conduct.text: Two preplanned interim analyses were conducted by a statistician associated with the independent data and safety monitoring board.
trial_conduct.quote: Two preplanned interim analyses were conducted by a statistician associated with the independent data and safety monitoring board.

trial_conduct.text: Primary efficacy outcome monitored with a Peto–Haybittle type stopping rule based on the log-rank P value.
trial_conduct.quote: The primary efficacy outcome was monitored with use of a Peto–Haybittle type of stopping rule based on the P value of the log-rank test.

criticisms.text: Subgroup observation should be interpreted with caution because P values were only marginally significant and it was one of several analyses.
criticisms.quote: the P value for this association and the P value for the interaction between enrollment status and therapy were only marginally significant, suggesting that this observation should be interpreted with caution, especially since this subgroup analysis was only one of several such analyses performed.

criticisms.text: Uncertainty about how the symptomatic vs asymptomatic classification could be implemented clinically because some asymptomatic patients had a history of symptoms or cardiovascular events.
criticisms.quote: it is unclear how such a classification could be implemented clinically, since some patients in the asymptomatic subgroup actually had a history of symptoms or cardiovascular events.
